9: Four NVIDIA Nemotron models on Nebius Token Factory, each sized to its step. Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (30B-A3B MoE) triages every message with thinking off: it is cheap and fast enough to run on everything ($0.18 per 1,000 messages alone), and its recall on ScamBench-MY was 99.3%. Nemotron 3 Super (120B-A12B) does verification planning and writes the verdict with reasoning on and a client-side budget: adding it cut false alarms by more than half versus Lightning alone (24.7% to 10.7%, significant on a paired bootstrap). Nemotron 3.5 Super VL reads forwarded screenshots (seniors forward screenshots more than text). Nemotron 3 Ultra (550B-A55B) is wired in as an optional second opinion; we measured it and it added no accuracy on our benchmark at +15% cost, so it is opt-in rather than default.
11: Out of the box, no fine-tuning (Nemotron is not in Token Factory's post-training base-model list, and we preferred measuring the base models honestly). Approach: (1) strict JSON-schema structured output on every call, with all fields required and bounded list lengths, because guided decoding skipped optional fields; (2) the reasoning toggle (chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking) off for triage, on with a token budget for planning/verdict; (3) prompts written as goals plus Malaysian-authority facts (SC vs SSM vs BNM, NSRC 997); (4) code-level policy under the model: regex backstop for entities, a floor that guarantees an official lookup per named entity, and evidence rebuilt only from verified tool hits so the model can never cite an unverified source.
12: We did not run other model families on our benchmark, so we make no head-to-head claim. Within the Nemotron family on ScamBench-MY (300 BM/EN/Manglish messages): keyword rules F1 0.763; Lightning alone F1 0.887 with 24.7% false alarms; Lightning + Super + Tavily + memory F1 0.939 with 10.7% false alarms; adding Ultra 0.936. Malay is not in Nemotron's documented languages, yet Lightning and Super each got 18/20 Malay/Manglish smoke-test messages right on day one; with the default pipeline, per-language F1 was 0.98 on Manglish, 0.94 on English and 0.93 on formal Malay.
13: (1) Breadth of the NVIDIA catalog on one OpenAI-compatible endpoint: four Nemotron tiers including the new 3.5 Super VL, swappable by config with fallback chains. (2) Structured output plus the thinking toggle, which made a tiered pipeline straightforward. (3) Price: the default pipeline is $2.20 per 1,000 messages, so a household costs about US$0.50 a year. (4) Onboarding: about 4 minutes from Google sign-in to a first Nemotron call, with billing active and credit already applied. (5) /v1/models as a startup health check that caught a wrong model ID for us.
16: (a) Document or warn that guided decoding omits optional (non-required) schema fields; it silently emptied our entity lists. (b) Enforce maxItems/maxLength in the guided decoder; Lightning sometimes looped inside list fields until max_tokens. (c) Consistent model-ID casing or case-insensitive lookup (nemotron-3-super vs Nemotron-3-Ultra vs Nemotron-3_5-Lightning vs Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL). (d) A spend cap and low-balance alert; HTTP 402 arrives mid-request. (e) A deprecation field on /v1/models. (f) A speech model on serverless; voice notes are how seniors forward things. (g) Serverless fine-tuning for Nemotron, as the product page suggests. Full write-up with exact symptoms: docs/FEEDBACK.md in the repo.
17: A Nemotron speech/omni model back on Token Factory serverless; documented Bahasa Malaysia (and wider Southeast Asian language) support with published evals; serverless LoRA fine-tuning for Nemotron 3.5 Lightning; and a small on-device Nemotron for Jetson so a family's triage can run fully at home.
22: Claude (Anthropic) was used heavily as a coding and research assistant to build this project: writing and debugging code, building the evaluation harness, drafting documentation, and recording demo footage. NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory is the only model family used at runtime by Jaga itself.
